faq.a: Jobs4DAE is a career portal for Diploma of Associate Engineering (DAE) students in Pakistan. It collects job openings, higher-education guides and AI tools for diploma holders.

faq.q: Which DAE fields does Jobs4DAE cover?
faq.a: Jobs4DAE covers the main DAE technologies, including electrical, mechanical, civil and electronics, with listings from government departments and private employers.
Jobs4DAE was founded by Abdul Rahman, a materials engineer and technical instructor in Lahore who trains diploma-level engineers.

Abdul Rahman is an AI-driven materials engineer and entrepreneur based in Lahore, Pakistan. He is a research engineer and senior instructor at the Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (PCSIR), holds BSc and MSc degrees in metallurgical and materials engineering from UET Lahore, and founded Connected 2 Future (C2F), EduCon and Jobs4DAE.

faq.q: What does Abdul Rahman specialize in?
faq.a: He specializes in physical and extractive metallurgy, materials informatics (machine learning and CALPHAD modeling), materials characterization with SEM/EDS, XRD and XRF, corrosion and protective coatings, and direct recycling of lithium-ion battery cathodes.

faq.q: Which companies has Abdul Rahman founded?
faq.a: Abdul Rahman founded Connected 2 Future (C2F), a digital agency for AI automation, web development and digital marketing, which he has led as CEO since 2020. He also founded EduCon, an education venture, and Jobs4DAE, a career portal for DAE students in Pakistan.

faq.q: Can I hire Abdul Rahman as a consultant?
faq.a: Yes. He advises on metallurgical failure analysis, SEM/EDS and XRD characterization, materials informatics workflows and mineral processing. You can book a 30-minute discovery call on the contact page.

His work includes machine learning-driven design of self-healing epoxy coatings with MgO-loaded ZIF-8 nanocontainers (submitted to a Springer Nature journal), hybrid generative machine learning for metal-organic frameworks (AIMS-2025), and an agentic AI digital twin for rare-earth materials discovery (MSE, DGM).
